defaults.permitted_development: Across Hampshire, hard surfacing is usually lowest risk on the planning permission route when drainage is handled properly, level changes stay modest and the work does not turn a soft frontage into a dominant engineered parking area. Frontage character and exposed plots can make drainage detail and surface appearance more visible than homeowners often expect.

rules.height_rules: Raised surfacing, retaining features and height or level changes can matter as much as the paving finish itself when councils assess hard-surface schemes in Hampshire.
rules.depth_rules: Surface coverage, front garden drainage and overall project extent are usually the deciding issues for hard surfacing across Hampshire, especially where large impermeable areas are proposed.
rules.boundary_rules: Frontage position, highway relationship and any linked access changes are often what make a hard-surfacing scheme more sensitive in Hampshire.
rules.roof_rules: For hard-surface projects, the design equivalent of a roof check is usually the drainage fall and discharge strategy rather than any vertical structure.
rules.materials_rules: Permeable, visually restrained finishes are usually easier to justify than broad impermeable paving that removes planting and dominates the frontage.

rules.permitted_development: In Basingstoke and Deane, hard surfacing is usually easiest to keep off the planning permission route where drainage is clear, levels stay sensible and the work does not turn the frontage into an over-engineered parking layout. restrictions.conservation_area: Hard surfacing in conservation areas within Basingstoke and Deane often faces a closer review where it changes the look of a visible frontage or removes established soft landscaping.
restrictions.listed_building: Works to the setting of a listed building in Basingstoke and Deane, including resurfacing and level changes, can need a more careful planning and heritage review.
